sources.name: DAN (Divers Alert Network)
sources.use_for: Diving medicine, fitness to dive, injuries, incident data and safety research.

sources.name: Google Scholar
sources.use_for: Peer-reviewed decompression, physiology and breathing-gas research.
sources.how_to_search: Search scholar.google.com with the topic and "diving" or "decompression", and prefer papers with a DOI.

sources.name: Rubicon Foundation
sources.use_for: Open archive of diving and hyperbaric research papers, including older Navy and journal reports.

sources.name: Diving and Hyperbaric Medicine
sources.use_for: Peer-reviewed diving and hyperbaric medicine journal of SPUMS and EUBS.

sources.name: TDI (Technical Diving International)
sources.use_for: Technical diving standards and course limits.
sources.notes: Site blocks automated checks; open it in a browser.

sources.name: PADI
sources.use_for: Recreational diving standards and course prerequisites.

sources.name: CMAS
sources.use_for: Federation standards, certification equivalences and fact sheets.

sources.name: InDEPTH (GUE)
sources.use_for: Technical diving articles by researchers and instructors, published by Global Underwater Explorers.
sources.notes: Magazine, not peer-reviewed; follow an article to the papers it cites.

sources.name: ScubaBoard
sources.use_for: Community experience, gear and dive site reports.
sources.notes: Opinions, verify against a vetted source.

sources.name: r/scuba wiki
sources.use_for: Community answers to common beginner questions, with links to further reading.
sources.how_to_search: Open the wiki index, then search r/scuba for the question.
sources.notes: Community-written; verify against a vetted source. Reddit renders it with JavaScript, so open it in a browser.
